1.א: The law of a Gentile who cooks on Shabbat—whether eating is forbidden because of bishul akum—see YD 113 and below §328.

4.ב: Hagahot Mordekhai 283b: something hard and unfit to eat except when softened may not be soaked on Shabbat because that completes the labor.
4.ג: This requires study—for above he cited Rambam that even soaking is forbidden unless fully cooked, and according to Rambam one should not distinguish liquid from dry (see above)—requires study.
4.ד: Mordekhai Kelal Kirah and R. Dan say our salt, prepared by boiling, need not worry—as the beraita “anything that came in hot water before Shabbat…”—yet one who is stringent is blessed.
4.ו: This does not appear correct from the Gemara and Tosafot Shabbat 42a—that for a washing vessel it is forbidden in every way per R. Shimon b. Menasya as Tosafot explain the conclusion following R. Shimon b. Menasya—and even so Tur follows Tosafot like R. Shimon; Ran elaborates. Piskei Mahari Weil is stringent to be careful even with a pot in every case.
